powershift

powershift helps an energy policy analyst preparing a briefing on a country’s electricity transition answer one question:

How much has a country’s electricity from one source changed between two years, and was that faster or slower than in other countries?

Countries are moving their electricity away from coal and towards wind and solar at very different speeds. Comparing the change in each source’s share of electricity shows which countries are moving fastest, and which sources are replacing which.

The package contains:

  • electricity_mix: Our World in Data estimates of how much of every country’s electricity came from nine sources, from 1985 to 2025.
  • share_change(): how much each source’s share changed between two years, in percentage points, with the result in words.
  • run_app(): a Shiny app that compares countries using these.

Documentation website: https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-tambatsmit/

Installation

Install the package from GitHub:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-tambatsmit")

Launch the app 

library(powershift)
run_app()

Choose a country to focus on, the countries to compare it with, a source of electricity and two years. The app reports how much that source’s share changed in each country, draws each country’s share over time, shows which sources rose and fell in the focus country, and explains any country without data for a year. The Guide tab explains every control and field.

Example

How much did coal’s share of electricity change from 2005 to 2025 in Australia, the United Kingdom, China and India?

library(powershift)

share_change(electricity_mix, from = 2005, to = 2025) |>
  dplyr::filter(
    source == "coal",
    country %in% c("Australia", "United Kingdom", "China", "India")
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(country, from_share, to_share, change)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 4
#>   country        from_share to_share change
#>   <chr>               <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 Australia            79.3   42.7   -36.6 
#> 2 China                79.2   54.3   -24.9 
#> 3 India                67.9   70.8     2.90
#> 4 United Kingdom       33.8    0.113 -33.7

Coal’s share of Australia’s electricity fell by about 37 percentage points, the largest fall of these four countries. The United Kingdom started lower and has almost stopped using coal, while India’s share rose slightly. The result column, not shown here, explains each case in words.

Data

  • Source: the Our World in Data energy dataset, based on Ember’s Yearly Electricity Data and the Energy Institute’s Statistical Review of World Energy.
  • Preparation: data-raw/electricity_mix.R reads data-raw/owid-energy-data.csv (downloaded on 30th October 2026), removes regional and income-group totals, and reshapes the share and generation columns for nine sources into one row per country, year and source. Run it from the package folder to rebuild data/electricity_mix.rda.
  • Licence: the data are available under the CC BY 4.0 licence. Cite them as “Our World in Data, based on Ember (2026) and the Energy Institute Statistical Review of World Energy (2025)”.
